# Disposable username and email component tests

Use only an isolated local backend on `127.0.0.1:3540/3541`, with a fresh database, no provider credentials, `--disable-beacon`, and `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` set in the backend before synchronization. Extract the catalog-selected auth archive to `authpkg` inside a disposable copy of this fixture and verify its bytes. Copy `email-fixture.ts.txt` to `authpkg/src/components/email/fixture.ts`; that seed/probe module is test-only and never enters the archive. Install dependencies in the disposable copy, then use `CONVEX_SELF_HOSTED_URL` and a disposable local admin key to run `convex dev --once --typecheck disable --codegen disable`. Run `python3 test.py` and stop only the backend you started. The sender is an inert local mutation and never contacts an email provider.

The test seeds 201 attributed verified emails and challenges, races real component completion/start with email fencing and races username setting with username fencing, verifies batch bounds, replay, an unaffected user, an attributed recovery challenge, and a retained unattributed custom challenge. The synthetic seed is deliberately not a product endpoint. The test does not prove all normal auth flows, a live email delivery, other components, or complete account deletion.

The combined product runner uses ports 3550/3551; run `python3 run-product.py` only when that pair is explicitly assigned and unoccupied. It verifies the installed auth bytes against the catalog-selected archive, then extracts that archive into a disposable directory, starts a fresh loopback backend, sets its telemetry gate before sync, runs the actual product operator handler with synthetic users and inert fixtures, and stops the owned process. It tests rollback after all four fences, concurrent batches, populated username/email/challenges, another user and re-registration denial. This fixture leaves unattributed challenge cleanup unverified and performs no provider operations.

The `email-flow` fixture mounts the real auth core, password, username and email components and the actual `setupEmailPassword` methods from the candidate. Its sender is a local internal mutation that stores synthetic messages only; the test reads the generated links from that private disposable database. In a separate disposable copy, install Convex and the exact local `.8` archive, start a fresh loopback backend, set `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` before sync, deploy the fixture, and run `python3 test.py`. The compiled package was exercised through its normal exports; a second run mounted the extracted candidate source. The test verifies unaffected signup, email verification, login, password change and recovery, plus rejection of a pending recovery, fresh recovery, login and password change for the fenced user. A recovery challenge is intentionally created with no user attribution: denial after verified-email removal does not establish deletion of that challenge. No email is delivered and no provider is contacted.
